summary: The ADDITIVE half of #8735's ask, applied only where the bundle already states the name at every position. #8735 asks for a `title` at each of 95 object structures the bundle restates and never titles; 50 of the 95 are UNDECIDABLE on the bundle's own evidence (survey/judgment.py) and titling them here would decide, for the protocol, a question only the protocol's authors can answer. This patch set holds the entries where there is nothing to decide: the bundle names every stating position with one and the same word, and no other entry of the layer derives it -- so the title is a transcription and not a judgment. TWO KINDS OF ENTRY, and the difference is whether the bundle has a path to the node already. For the first, its own $refs reach one of the stating positions, so a second document would give one subject a second name and the keyword is the whole of what is missing. For the four titles added 2026-11-05 -- URL Macro Declaration, Explicit Collection Selector, Publisher Placement Reference, Unlocalized Creative Asset -- no $ref reaches any position: each is a NARROWING of a document the bundle does name, restated at two to five positions and titled at none, and the bundle's own precedent for that shape is core/forecast-rate-range.json, a titled document holding `allOf: [{$ref: core/forecast-range.json}, {low/mid/high maximum: 1}]`. So an extraction is the stronger ask for those four and is filed beside this one; what the title claims, and the whole of what it claims, is that the restating positions are ONE subject, which nothing in the bundle says today. Annotation-only on both kinds: no keyword a draft-07 validator acts on moves at any pointer of any document, which codegen.patch.seen_by_a_validator checks over all 1,054 portable documents. THE BUNDLE THIS SET IS APPLIED TO IS THE PUBLISHED (BUILT) ONE, AND FOR ONE POSITION THAT MATTERS. core/assets/display-tag-asset.json#/oneOf/0/properties/macro_declarations/items is a composed `allOf` in the published bundle and a bare `{properties: {location: ...}}` overlay in upstream's own source, where the build merges it with the root's `items: {$ref: core/macro-declaration.json}`. So the upstream ask for URL Macro Declaration ranges over the FOUR source positions that state the composed node (daast-tracker, pixel-tracker, url and vast tracker assets) and this set titles five, the fifth being that merge's output. The same overlay form at core/assets/daast-asset.json#/oneOf/0 and core/assets/vast-asset.json#/oneOf/0 is titled by NEITHER: the node's own text says nothing about a macro declaration, so a title there would be a claim it does not support (adcp-client-python-e4z).

additions.names: the contact point where a data subject contests an automated decision
additions.defect: the bundle states this structure at two positions in two documents -- brand.json#/definitions/data_subject_contestation and core/brand-ref.json#/properties/data_subject_contestation -- calls both of them `data_subject_contestation`, joins them by no $ref, and titles neither. Its own $refs reach the first, so the bundle already has a path and a pointer for this subject and writes the structure out again anyway.
additions.why_not_an_extraction: the bundle already names this node: a $ref inside brand.json reaches #/definitions/data_subject_contestation. Extracting it would give one subject a SECOND name, which is the one thing naming it was for. The keyword is the whole of what is missing.
additions.why_this_string: `data_subject_contestation` is the word the bundle itself writes at both positions, spelled by the project's own naming rule. docs/plan/architecture.md, 'WHEN A NAME IS THE BUNDLE'S': 'the property name the positions share | stated | take it'. Nothing here is lifted from a description.

additions.names: one macro-token occurrence whose location is the asset's own locator `url` field
additions.defect: the bundle states `{allOf: [{$ref: core/macro-declaration.json}, {properties: {location: {properties: {field: {const: "url"}}}}}]}` at five positions in five core/assets documents, names every one of them `macro_declarations`, joins the five by no $ref and titles none of them. It NAMES the base -- core/macro-declaration.json, titled "Macro Declaration" -- and leaves the narrowed subject anonymous, so a reader and a generator meet the same restriction five times with nothing to tell them it is one restriction. core/assets/display-tag-asset.json is the proof that the narrowing is a subject and not an accident: its three oneOf branches narrow the SAME base to `url`, to `markup` and to `{ad_request_url, clickthrough_url}`, which is a family of three the bundle titles nowhere.
additions.why_not_an_extraction: core/forecast-rate-range.json is the bundle's own precedent for extracting a narrowing of a named document into a titled document of its own, so an extraction is defensible here and is the stronger ask (filed beside this one). It is not THIS patch set's kind: #8735 asks for a `title` and nothing else, and an addition is the one override that leaves every $ref and every acceptance keyword of all 1,054 documents where they are. The title is what identifies the five positions as one subject; which document the subject should live in is a second question and upstream's to answer.
additions.why_this_string: `url` is the word the narrowing itself pins (`location.field: {const: "url"}`) and "Macro Declaration" is the title the bundle gives the base at core/macro-declaration.json, so the string is the bundle's own two words and a modifier read off the one keyword that distinguishes the subject -- the same form core/forecast-rate-range.json takes over core/forecast-range.json ("Forecast Range" -> "Forecast Rate Range"). It is what a person says about this node: a URL macro declaration. Nothing is minted from the structure: `ObjLocationFieldUrl` is the compiler's placeholder form and is not a name.

additions.names: a collection selector obliged to name the collection_ids it selects, rather than the domain-only form that grants all of them
additions.defect: the bundle states `{allOf: [{$ref: core/collection-selector.json}, {required: ["collection_ids"]}]}` at three positions in three documents -- core/canonical-product.json, core/collection-selection.json and core/product.json -- names every one of them `collections`, joins the three by no $ref and titles none of them. core/collection-selector.json's own description states that omitting `collection_ids` IS a second form ("the bulk-grant form for authorization scoping"), and all three positions say in prose that this form is not the one they accept; so the bundle distinguishes two subjects in three descriptions and gives the narrower one no name.
additions.why_not_an_extraction: same answer as the entry above: an extraction is the stronger ask and is filed beside this one. What this entry claims is only that the three positions are ONE subject, which is what a title says and what nothing in the bundle says today.
additions.why_this_string: "Collection Selector" is the title the bundle gives the base at core/collection-selector.json, and `explicit` is the bundle's own word for the distinction at all three positions: "explicit collection_ids" in core/canonical-product.json and core/product.json, "explicit collection_ids" again in core/collection-selection.json. A reader meets the base's own contrast -- explicit selection against bulk grant -- in the name. Not lifted from a description as a sentence: one word that the three positions and the base all write.

additions.names: a placement reference whose publisher_domain is present, so the publisher's own adagents.json is the authority that owns the placement_id
additions.defect: the bundle states `{allOf: [{$ref: core/placement-ref.json}, {required: ["publisher_domain"]}]}` at two positions in two documents, names both of them `placement_refs`, joins the two by no $ref and titles neither. The narrowing is the authority question the bundle itself raises: core/placement-ref.json admits a reference with no publisher_domain ("receivers MAY interpret the ID relative to the enclosing single-publisher product") and core/placement-identity.json, titled "Placement Identity", exists because "the discriminator names which authority owns placement_id". core/placement-selection.json's own description puts this subject beside that one, in an anyOf, and calls it "Legacy publisher refs" -- so the bundle names one arm of a two-arm choice and leaves the other anonymous.
additions.why_not_an_extraction: same answer as the entries above. Note that this position is a BRANCH, where the project's own keyword table makes a `title` the branch class's NAME -- so for this one entry the title is rendered and not only recorded, which is the clearest case that nothing here needs a second document to be a name.
additions.why_this_string: "Placement Reference" is the title the bundle gives the base at core/placement-ref.json, and `publisher` is what the required key names: publisher_domain, whose presence is exactly the fact that the publisher is the authority. The bundle writes "publisher-catalog placements" at the base and "Legacy publisher refs" at the selection position. `Legacy` is deliberately NOT in the string: it dates the subject rather than naming it, and the same structure is the only accepted form at core/package-format-snapshot.json, where nothing is legacy.

additions.names: a creative asset offered on the inline-upload path, which may not carry a localization block
additions.defect: the bundle states `{allOf: [{$ref: core/creative-asset.json}, {not: {required: ["localization"]}}]}` at two positions in two documents -- media-buy/package-request.json and media-buy/package-update.json -- names both of them `creatives`, joins the two by no $ref and titles neither. Both positions state the reason in prose and state it the same way ("Native localization is not accepted on this path; use sync_creatives before assigning the library creative"), so the bundle asserts one restriction twice in English and zero times as a name.
additions.why_not_an_extraction: same answer as the entries above.
additions.why_this_string: "Creative Asset" is the title the bundle gives the base at core/creative-asset.json, and the whole of the narrowing is that `localization` is forbidden -- so `unlocalized` names the one fact that distinguishes this subject from the base, in a word a person uses. "Inline Creative Asset" was the alternative and is rejected: `creatives` on a package request is the FIELD's role, inline-upload is the path the field belongs to, and neither is a property of the type -- the same reason the `result` entry of adcp-client-python-s44.1 is held rather than titled.
